Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family member has a new job and has shared some initial excitement about it with their relatives.
Expectation2: Respect the mentor's time and availability.
Situation2: The mentor arranged a short meeting in an otherwise packed day.
Story:
I glanced at my phone, a message from my daughter lighting up the screen: “Dad, can you call tonight? Sam just started his new job and wants to tell you all about it!” I smiled, picturing my grandson’s eager face, remembering how much it meant to him when I listened to his stories. Family always came first, and I prided myself on being the grandparent who never missed a moment, who always picked up the phone.

But then, my calendar pinged—a reminder of the meeting my mentor had squeezed in for me. She was incredibly busy, and I knew how rare it was for her to carve out even fifteen minutes. I’d been waiting for this chance to ask her advice on a project that could shape my career. I couldn’t risk seeming ungrateful or unreliable.

My heart thudded as I weighed the two calls, both scheduled for the same time. I felt torn, the warmth of family expectation pulling me one way, the pressure to honor my mentor’s time tugging the other. I stared at my phone, caught between the voices of those who believed in me, unsure which one I’d have to disappoint.
